definitions.definition: ell=max(λ,0), regarded as a natural number (the integer-to-natural conversion λ.toNat). This definition imposes no range condition on λ.
J=Fin(ell+1), identified with the integers i satisfying 0≤i≤ell.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, X_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ x^r, with x^0=Id_V. Factorials are the usual products, with 0!=1.

definitions.type: sequence of complex-linear endomorphisms of V
definitions.definition: For each natural r, Y_r=(r! : ℂ)⁻¹ y^r, with y^0=Id_V.
For i∈J set e_i=Y_i(v)=y^i(v)/i!; the index i denotes its natural value.

definitions.type: integer subalgebra of the universal enveloping algebra of sl₂(ℂ)
definitions.definition: U_ℤ is generated over ℤ by the divided powers x^r/r! and y^r/r! for all natural r. Its action on V is generated by the operators X_r,Y_r. Operator stability under this algebra means stability under every generator.

V_K=M⊗_ℤ K, with K acting on the second factor. This is the original V(K). For any f∈End_ℤ(M), f⊗Id_K acts by u⊗a↦f(u)⊗a. The original induced x,y,h actions are the tensor extensions of their restrictions to M; h|M=(x|M)(y|M)−(y|M)(x|M).
Q=K⊗_ℤ M, with K acting on the first factor.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, A_r=X_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every X_r preserves M. In particular A_1=x|M and A_0=Id_M.

definitions.type: sequence of integer-linear endomorphisms of M
definitions.definition: For every natural r, B_r=Y_r|M, the restriction to M. Its construction requires the original admissibility hypothesis that every Y_r preserves M. In particular B_1=y|M and B_0=Id_M.
For i,j∈J let s_ij=j!(ell−j)! A_(ell−i) B_ell A_ell B_(ell−j), with integer scalar multiplication. Products of endomorphisms mean composition with the right factor first.
d=(ell!:K), the image of the natural factorial under ℤ→K. No nonvanishing is assumed by this definition.

For f∈End_ℤ(M), Fext(f)=Id_K⊗f is the scalar extension obtained by the balanced tensor construction; on pure tensors Fext(f)(a⊗u)=a⊗f(u). Its additivity, multiplicativity, unitality and compatibility with integer scalars are conclusions to prove when used.
For i,j∈J define U_ij=d⁻¹ Fext(s_ij). Here inverse is the total field operation, with 0⁻¹=0; no matrix-unit identity or invertibility is granted by this definition.

τ is the balanced tensor map specified by τ(u⊗a)=a⊗u. The scalar action on V_K is on its second factor and on Q on its first factor. Bijectivity and operator intertwining are assertions to prove, rather than part of this definition.

inputs.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.

For every integer basis (b_i)_(i∈J) of M, the vectors 1⊗b_i form a K-basis of Q. In particular Q is finite dimensional, dim_K Q=ell+1>0, and Q is nonzero. The map τ:V_K→Q is a K-linear isomorphism, with inverse a⊗u↦u⊗a. For every f∈End_ℤ(M), τ∘(f⊗Id_K)=Fext(f)∘τ. Consequently V_K is also nonzero of K-dimension ell+1. In particular this intertwining applies to f=A_1=x|M, f=B_1=y|M, and f=h|M=A_1 B_1−B_1 A_1.

binders.type: integer basis of M indexed by J

inputs.statement: One has d≠0, U_ij U_kl=δ_jk U_il for all i,j,k,l∈J, and ∑_(i∈J)U_ii=Id_Q, with δ_jk=1 if j=k and 0 otherwise. Every K-linear subspace W⊆Q satisfying Fext(A_1)(W)⊆W and Fext(B_1)(W)⊆W satisfies U_ij(W)⊆W for all i,j∈J. This holds for ell=0 and uses no distinctness of reduced h-eigenvalues or algebraic closure of K.

For every field F, positive natural n, finite-dimensional F-vector space T with dim_F T=n, and endomorphisms C_ij∈End_F(T) indexed by i,j∈Fin n satisfying C_ij C_kl=δ_jk C_il for all indices and ∑_i C_ii=Id_T, every F-linear subspace Z⊆T preserved by all C_ij is zero or all T. Here δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise, and products mean composition with the right factor acting first.

output.statement:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

locals.declaration: Let W be an arbitrary K-linear subspace of V_K.
Set Z=τ(W), the image subspace under the K-linear map τ.

argument.text:
Under H001, λ≥0 implies (ell:ℤ)=λ. Thus ell

0, and τ:V_K→Q is a K-linear isomorphism intertwining every lattice endomorphism with its Fext extension. In particular the x,y,h actions are identified exactly as stated in N003.

produces.statement: V_K is nonzero; dim_K Q=ell+1>0; τ is a K-linear isomorphism intertwining the original x,y,h actions with Fext(A_1), Fext(B_1), and Fext(A_1 B_1−B_1 A_1) respectively.

argument.text: Let W be arbitrary and temporarily assume L1: W is preserved by the original induced x,y,h actions. Define Z=τ(W). It is a K-subspace because τ is K-linear. For every w∈W, N003 gives Fext(A_1)τ(w)=τ applied to the induced x-action on w, and Fext(B_1)τ(w)=τ applied to the induced y-action on w. Both results belong to Z by L1. Hence Z is preserved by the two required endomorphisms of Q.

Apply the invariant-subspace implication of N004 to Z using F002. It gives U_ij(Z)⊆Z for every i,j∈J. The same N004 supplies all matrix-unit multiplication relations and ∑_i U_ii=Id_Q. Apply N005 with its field F=K, positive n=ell+1, T=Q, C=U and subspace Z. Its finite dimensionality and dimension premises are N003, and J=Fin(ell+1) by D002. All remaining premises are those just supplied by N004. Thus Z=0 or Z=Q.

If Z=0, then every w∈W has τ(w)=0, so injectivity of τ gives w=0 and W=0. If Z=Q, for any vector of V_K its τ-image belongs to Z and hence equals τ(w) for some w∈W; injectivity makes that vector equal to w. Thus W=V_K. Apply these alternatives to F003 to get W=0 or W=V_K.

Discharge L1 and universally quantify W. Together with nonzero V_K from F001, this proves the complete target under the original H001. Stability under x,y,h is equivalent to stability under their K-linear combinations, the stated Chevalley Lie action; the proof only needed x and y. The irreducibility assumption on the complex V and the h-stability condition remain in H001 and the target even though not all their strength was needed. All steps allow ell=0 and p=2, and only field operations in K were used, so no algebraic closure hypothesis has been added.
